q: Which church is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
n: The Baroque Churches inscription has four churches.

q: Which is the oldest stone church in Manila, its parish founded in 1571?
n: The present stone church dates from 1607.

q: Which is the oldest stone church in Bohol, built by the Jesuits?
n: Baclayon, 1727.

q: Which church is the first all-steel church in Asia?
n: Prefabricated steel, 1891.

q: The National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help, one of Asia's most visited churches, is commonly called:
n: Run by the Redemptorists.

q: Which church is the seat of the Archdiocese of Manila and the sixth cathedral on its site since 1581?
n: Rebuilt in 1958.

q: The Minor Basilica of the Holy Child in Cebu City is also called the:
o: Basílica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebú
n: Founded in 1565.

q: Now the Basilica of the Immaculate Conception, its first builder was Bishop Domingo de Salazar and its present architect Fernando Ocampo. Which church is it?
n: Ocampo rebuilt it in 1954–58.

q: Which Iloilo church, a 1973 national landmark, has a façade carved with coconut trees and St. Christopher carrying the Child?
n: A UNESCO site since 1993.

q: Which church, first built by the Augustinian Fr. Miguel Murguia, has a huge bell cast from about 70 sacks of donated coins?
n: Asia's largest church bell.

q: Declared a national landmark in 1973, what is the first all-steel building constructed in the Philippines?
n: San Sebastian Church is the all-steel landmark declared in 1973.

q: Which Ilocos Norte church is known for Earthquake Baroque and huge buttresses and is a UNESCO site?
n: St. Augustine, Paoay.

q: When was the United Architects of the Philippines founded?
n: Formed from three older groups.

q: In what year was the United Architects of the Philippines (UAP) registered with the SEC?
n: UAP was formed and registered in 1975 (it marked its 50th year in 2025).

q: When was the first UAP president inducted?
n: After the 1974 founding.

q: Who was the first Charter President of UAP in 1975?
n: UAP history references name Norberto M. Nuke as the first national president when UAP was formed in 1975.

q: Who was the first woman president of both the UAP and ARCASIA?
n: Yolanda David-Reyes was UAP's first woman national president and ARCASIA's first woman chair.

q: Who was the first president of the Philippine Architects Society (later renamed Philippine Institute of Architects — PIA)?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was the first president of the Philippine Architects Society (1933); Tomás Mapúa followed in 1935.

q: Besides the LPA and APGA, which group joined to form the UAP?
n: PIA, LPA and APGA merged in 1974.

q: Which UAP award honors outstanding Filipino architects?
n: The UAP's highest honor.

q: What was the National Museum of Fine Arts building originally?
n: Old Congress building.

q: Who was the Filipino architect responsible for the design of the building now known as the National Museum?
n: Juan Arellano reworked and completed the Legislative Building, now the National Museum.

q: Under the Burnham Plan, what was the building now housing the National Museum meant to be?
n: It was redesigned for the legislature.

q: In 2015, the National Museum underwent major renovation works under which architectural firm?
n: Dominic Galicia's firm, Galicia Architects, led the 2015 National Museum renovation.

q: What is the name of the central theme of the renovation and retrofitting works done at the National Museum?
n: "Tree of Life" was the central theme of the National Museum renovation.

q: The Coconut Palace by Francisco Mañosa is also called:
n: Built of coconut materials.

q: What is the dominant shape of the floor plan of Tahanang Pilipino, resembling a sliced coconut when served?
n: The Coconut Palace (Tahanang Pilipino) is octagonal, like a trimmed coconut, under a salakot-shaped roof.

q: Who was the architect of the church known as Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage in Antipolo?
n: José L. de Ocampo designed the present Antipolo Cathedral (built 1948–1954).

q: Who is the architect behind the art and sports center located in San Juan, Manila?
n: JAGNUS Design Studio (Sonny Sunga and Arnold Austria) is based at, and designed, the RONAC Art Center in San Juan.

q: What is the name of the development in San Juan designed by JAGNUS Design Studio that combines art, retail, and sports?
n: JAGNUS Design Studio designed the RONAC Art Center on Ortigas Avenue, San Juan.

q: What style is the Manila Cathedral?
n: Fernando Ocampo's rebuild.

q: Manila Cathedral is dedicated to:
n: Minor Basilica of the Immaculate Conception.

q: When was the last major retrofit of Manila Cathedral completed?
n: Reopened in April 2014.

q: The Grand Mosque in Cotabato was a gift from His Highness, the Sultan of Brunei, to the people of Cotabato. Who was the architect of this structure?
n: Palafox Associates designed the Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Masjid (Grand Mosque) in Cotabato City.

q: What color are the domes of the Grand Mosque in Cotabato?
n: The Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah Masjid.

q: The church known as the Basilica Minore del Santo Nifio is primarily constructed from which type of stone?
n: The Basílica del Santo Niño is built of coral (Mactan) stone.

q: What is the oldest documented house in the Philippines, in Cebu City?
n: Casa de los Jesuitas.

q: When was the Jesuit House in Cebu City built?
n: Dated by an inscription.

q: What is the large church on the Ateneo de Manila campus?
n: Completed in 2002.

q: Who designed the Church of the Gesù at Ateneo?
n: Jose Pedro Recio and Carmelo Casas.
